extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in international affairs and United Nations diplomacy
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper/press report covering United Nations Assembly and political committee debates (Western 12-point peace proposal, Soviet counterproposals, related diplomatic events).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refrain from threatening or using force contrary to the United Nations charter
rubrics_metrics.description: Refrain from threatening or using force contrary to the United Nations charter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item #1 in the U.S.-British 'twelve-point Western plan'/'Peace Essentials' presented to the UN political committee; positioned as a foundational requirement for postwar peace and as a response to Soviet-Western tensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refrain from threats or acts impairing another state's independence or fomenting civil strife
rubrics_metrics.description: Refrain from any threats or acts aimed at impairing the independence or integrity of any country or fomenting civil strife.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item #2 of the Western essentials; framed as a prohibition on interference in other nations' sovereignty and internal affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carry out international agreements in good faith
rubrics_metrics.description: Carry out in good faith all international agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item #3 of the Western essentials; emphasizes honoring treaty commitments as a pillar of peaceful international relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Afford UN bodies full co-operation and free access
rubrics_metrics.description: Afford all United Nations bodies full co-operation and free access in the performance of tasks assigned to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item #4 of the Western essentials; calls for member states to provide cooperation and access to UN organs carrying out assigned tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security Council: exercise restraint in using the veto
rubrics_metrics.description: Security Council and exercise restraint in using the veto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented in the same set of 'essentials' (fragmented in text); urges that veto power be exercised with restraint to enable UN effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote full freedom of political and religious expression and respect fundamental rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote full freedom of political and religious expression and full respect for all other fundamental rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears among the 'Peace Essentials'; frames human rights and freedoms as necessary components of peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote higher standards of living through national and international co-operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote nationally and through international co-operation efforts to achieve higher standards of living for all peoples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item in the Western 12-point proposal emphasizing socio-economic measures (improving standards of living) as part of a peace program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove barriers denying free exchange of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove barriers which deny people the free exchange of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item #7 in the Western plan; positions free information exchange as an essential condition for peace and understanding among nations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participate fully in the work of the United Nations
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate fully in the work [of the United Nations].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fragmented in the text (appears as item #8); urges full participation in UN activities as part of multinational problem-solving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-operate to achieve international regulation of conventional armaments
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-operate in attaining effective international regulation of conventional armaments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among the Western essentials (appears as item #10); calls for international steps to regulate non‑nuclear armaments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agree to exercise national sovereignty jointly with other states
rubrics_metrics.description: Agree to exercise national sovereignty jointly with other [states].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fragmentary in the copy (appears in proximity to other numbered essentials); expresses a principle of pooled/joint sovereignty in certain international matters as part of peace arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Urge the great powers to broaden their co-operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Urge the five big powers to broaden their co-operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item #12 (part of the Western essentials) calling on the major powers to expand cooperation — context implies in areas such as atomic energy and security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call on Soviet Union to stop 'campaign of hate' and engage in direct talks
rubrics_metrics.description: Call on Soviet Union to stop its 'campaign of hate,' meet with the West, lift the Iron Curtain and discuss common problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of United States delegate Warren R. Austin's framing of the Western proposal — political/diplomatic behavioral demands directed at the USSR intended to reduce tensions and enable joint problem-solving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resume UN Atomic Energy Commission meetings and continue talks among atomic powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Resume suspended meetings of the United Nations Atomic Energy Commission and continue talks among the atomic powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced in the report that the political committee approved a plan to continue talks on atomic curbs; presented as a procedural step to work toward atomic controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit atomic weapons and establish conventions/controls (Soviet proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition of atomic weapons and a convention setting up controls; a pact among the five powers to control atomic energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes elements of the Soviet Foreign Minister Vishinsky's proposal (as reported): an insistence on prohibition and multilateral control mechanisms; the Western delegation rejected the Soviet text while debating the atomic issue.
